content.text: No liquidated damages, penalty, or termination-fee provision exists anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 12.3 Additional Termination Rights by AbbVie. AbbVie may terminate this Agreement in its entirety, or on a country or other jurisdiction -by-country or other jurisdiction basis, for any or no reason, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Harpoon.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/exit fee payable by AbbVie (our party), which meets the preferred position. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "forfeit" and minimum-payment language returned nothing, and a full read of Article 12 confirms it: AbbVie may terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice under Section 12.3 with no termination payment, and the termination consequences (Sections 12.6–12.8, 12.10) are limited to licence reversion, product wind-down and payment of amounts already accrued for pre-termination milestones/Net Sales — ordinary accrued consideration, not a liquidated sum. All AbbVie payment obligations located (upfront, milestones, royalties in Sections 6.1–6.5) are ordinary purchase consideration. Noted but not a deviation: Section 6.10 default interest on late payments is expressly mutual ("If any payment due to either Party ... such paying Party shall pay interest thereon"), and interest of this kind is a time-value remedy rather than liquidated damages; the rate itself is redacted ([***]), so we cannot confirm it is commercially standard, but nothing suggests a punitive uplift and it applies equally to Harpoon. Section 12.9 preserves ordinary law and equity remedies mutually rather than fixing a pre-agreed sum. No redline required.
